lessons.title: Sensing light, sound, touch and water

scenes.say: Euglena’s eyespot near its front shades a light receptor. The cell can use changing illumination to orient its swimming.

The cochlea in the inner ear contains hair cells that convert vibrations into signals sent along the auditory nerve. Vibrissae are sensitive whiskers. Bending a whisker stimulates receptors near its root, helping a rat sense nearby surfaces.
Hydrotropism is directional growth in response to moisture. A growing root can bend towards wetter soil.
JAMB asks how Euglena senses light direction, where hearing receptors are found, and whether growth towards water is hydrotropism. Blue arrows show movement of a stimulus or the direction of growth.

quickCheck.prompt: Where are the hearing receptor hair cells?
quickCheck.feedback: Hearing receptor hair cells are inside the cochlea, in the organ of Corti.
